summary: AI operations builder urges daily system checks, independent cross-vendor AI checkers with human review, and same-day re-checks and practice notification when underlying models change.

Cloud medical software developer flags gaps: multiple-function products, cybersecurity, human factors, RAG validation layers, statistical acceptance criteria, agentic controls, and third-party foundation model change management.

Supports competency-based evaluation and risk-tiered monitoring, proposes modular component-level regulation and foundation model provenance tracking, largely promoting the PrimordiaOS platform as an example.

Device professional endorses key paper positions and urges data exposure as a risk dimension, limited premarket-postmarket tradeoffs, mandatory foundation model transparency, version pinning, and standard-of-care comparators.

Radiation oncologist argues competency should be task-specific and consequence-sensitive, with specialist comparators, error detectability in risk, independent adjudication, trigger-based monitoring, and agentic autonomy boundaries.
Pharma CMC professional urges reusing existing FDA terminology and drug-side mechanisms (V&V 40, ICH Q12, MDDT, Part 11) and clarifying treatment of GenAI in combination products.

Venture studio urges least-burdensome oversight favoring postmarket monitoring, separating clinical validity from utility, voluntary third-party programs, CLIA-style precedents, and protecting early-stage company market entry.
Physician analyzes CMS and state AI coverage-decision laws to show duties fall on deployers, proposing supplier-information mechanisms and a three-question test for accountability assignments.
Health system supply chain researcher argues institutions cannot inventory or trace GenAI devices, so their monitoring role should be receiving and reporting, with tiered public Master Files.

Surgeon urges surgical GenAI risk assessment to include irreversibility, time to harm, and rescue, with human-AI team testing, no postmarket tradeoff for invasive actions, and control-based accountability.

Brief comment recommends clear performance metrics, expanded risk dimensions, retraining documentation, proactive drift monitoring, and risk-based revalidation triggers within a continuous lifecycle framework.
Strongly supports the framework and asks for streamlined pathways for HCP-supervised tools like scribing and imaging second-reads, operational Master Files, supervisory agents, and flexible PCCPs.
Clinical engineer urges requirements for safe failure during dependency outages, GenAI cybersecurity, serviceability and repair access, lifecycle support, and inclusion of HTM professionals.

Proposes a write-authority partition limiting what generative components can record or initiate, as an auditable basis for risk placement, benchmarking, change triggers, monitoring, and agentic gating.

Argues benchmark construct validity requires measurement-system qualification, including null self-comparisons, validated multi-turn windows, separate escalation error rates, and change-type-scaled re-benchmarking with versioned adjudicators.

org: The Christman AI Project and Robotics Division
summary: Endorses benchmark elements but asks for specified in-session sampling position, a new input-integrity safety element, broader prompt-injection coverage, and independent provenance records.
